evals.name: config-and-input-given
evals.prompt: Show me the transfer function for ~/recon/phase_3d.yml using the data at ~/data/cells.zarr/0/0/0.
evals.expected_output: Runs `wo compute-tf` with the given input position and config, writes ./otf.zarr, opens it with `wo view` without blocking, and reports the path.
expectations: The agent runs `wo compute-tf -i ~/data/cells.zarr/0/0/0 -c ~/recon/phase_3d.yml -o` with an output zarr path.
The agent does not use a nonexistent `calc-tf` subcommand.
The agent launches `wo view` on the transfer function so it does not block further commands.
The agent does not render a PNG or matplotlib figure of the transfer function.
The agent reports the output zarr path and that napari is open.

evals.name: missing-inputs
evals.prompt: I want to see how changing the condenser NA changes the OTF for my phase config.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the config path and an input position path before running anything, and explains that the input is only used for its ZYX shape.
expectations: The agent asks for the config path and the input position path.
The agent explains that `wo compute-tf` reads only the array shape from the input.
The agent does not run `wo compute-tf` before it has both paths.

evals.name: 2d-singular-system
evals.prompt: Compute and show the OTF for my 2D phase config ~/recon/phase_2d.yml with ~/data/bf.zarr/0/0/0. Why does it look different from the 3D one?
evals.expected_output: Runs the two calls, then explains that 2D reconstructions store a singular system (U, S, Vh) that `wo view` combines back into the absorption and phase transfer functions.
expectations: The agent runs `wo compute-tf` and then `wo view` on the result.
The agent explains that a 2D transfer function is stored as a singular system that `wo view` reconstructs as H = U diag(S) Vh.
The agent mentions that the 2D phase view shows absorption and phase transfer functions.
